text: We had an appointment with the doctor at 4:00 PM for laser papilloma removal. We arrived on time, received anesthesia, and waited for the doctor. At 5:20 PM, a nurse came in and said, “Sorry, the doctor didn’t come in today.” We waited for almost an hour and a half. We simply wasted our time. I do not recommend coming here if you respect yourself and value your time.

Wow!  Time medicine is so far ahead of the United States. Day I saw Dr Siriwit Wongsakul, a dermatologist at the ram Skin Clinic, for my first ever skin check. He is really knowledgeable and had such a great bedside manner. He examined me for anything precancerous on my skin, and found a few places. After this very thorough examination, he froze off the trouble spots in a completely fast and painless procedure. And I also had him and the great nursing staff here remove a skin tag. My appointment was at 2:00 p.m., and I was promptly ushered in to see the doctor at that time, and the whole thing was finished within 30 minutes. This is a very modern and new facility, where everyone speaks English. I now have a local dermatologist! I made this appointment 2 days ago. In the United States I would have waited weeks for this appointment to see a specialist. For everything that I had done today including some antibiotic ointment to put on the places where he froze, I paid $3,500 baht, or about 100 US dollars. In the US this procedure and appointment would have been at least 10 times that. I strongly recommend Dr. Wongsakul, and I already have my check- up appointment set for next year.  Thank you Dr. Siriwit and staff at the RAM Skin Clinic!

I don’t recommend this place. The doctor seems very sloppy. Messy hair and bare feet. The consultation only lasts about 2 minutes, and the consultation fee is far from cheap. I’ve been there twice to treat my acne problem, and there’s been no improvement at all. I had twice vascular laser treatment, and the experience was terrible. The nurse didn’t assist with anything—I had to clean my own face with low-quality tissue from the restroom. After the treatment, my face was red and swollen, but they didn’t provide an ice pack or any calming gel to reduce the redness. Overall, I’m very disappointed and will not be going back.

Saw a skin specialist here after 4 weeks of itching in full body and having consulted a doctor in another hospital. Really disappointed that after having suffered for a month the doctor isn't thinking outside the box for what could be the root cause and just prescribed further ten days with antihistamines. It is a common sense that until the cause is found the symptoms would not go away. Further the medication was charged at double the price 466 THB for 10 pills which is available in pharmacy for 225 THB. My confidence in this hospital died completely when they asked me to come after two days to review the blood reports and pay the same doctor fee again. I think the following up with the doctor for reports should not be another consultation fee and it's unethical practice because I already paid for the doctor and blood tests during my first visit. What is more upsetting that not all the reports be available in two days then why book follow up in two days?

With this type of business practice, I cancelled my appointment and found a local, old and experienced skin specialist. It was a humanly experience to meet that man who immediately thought could be the problem from my initial blood reports and gave prescription. He even suggested places to visit in the city and hiking points. I think a doctor should make patient feel at ease first. I am hoping this will work because just taking antihistamines from these big hospitals is not curing the problem at all. Further the medication should be cheaper in big hospitals and not make business.

I feel the patient care and medicare are dead in big branded hospitals.

To be honest, I was a little disappointed.
I love Chiang Mai Ram hospital, so I went to their skin clinic for a skin cancer check up (just to check all my moles to make sure nothing had turned bad).

The doctor proceeded to show me what bad moles looked like and advised me to 'check myself'.

After which I was slapped with an 800thb bill.

(Usually, a dermatologist would check over every mole with a special eye piece and inspect the health of each mole - that what I was expecting, not the above).

Perhaps they don't understand / do skin cancer check ups over here, but in Australia, it's a very prominent and common thing.

I won't be going there again.

I attended the dermatology department for a skin/mole check and had a small biopsy done during the appointment. Getting an appointment was straight forward and the staff were prompt with their replies.
The procedure itself was completed, but overall my experience was disappointing.
The communication and aftercare process were not as clear as I expected. I was initially told to return in person for the biopsy results and stitch removal. After I contacted the hospital, they were able to email the pathology result to me instead. I appreciated that this was possible, but I wish this option had been explained upfront, as it saved me both time and additional cost.
I also found the itemised bill difficult to understand. For a small biopsy, the bill appeared to include multiple glove charges — around 10 pairs/items of gloves in total, including surgical and latex gloves, about 287 baht total — as well as 150 ml of saline, listed at 142 baht, which I did not recall being used or receiving for wound care. There was also a nylon suture item charged at 409 baht. I contacted the hospital to ask for clarification and was told the query would be forwarded to the department head, but I did not receive any follow-up explanation.
During the consultation, comments about sun damage and sunscreen made me feel quite self-conscious. I understand that sun exposure is medically important, hence why I do regular skin checks, but I would have appreciated a more neutral and supportive explanation.
Overall, while the clinical procedure was completed, I felt the communication, billing clarity, and aftercare guidance could have been much better.

There was someone to guide you from the moment you entered. Before 5 PM, you can request a Chinese translator free of charge. I went to see a dentist, and the doctor was very gentle! Highly recommended! I'm from Taiwan.

I had laser treatment here. Unlike other beauty clinics that often try to sell you packages you're not interested in, this clinic is very clean, and the doctors and nurses are very attentive. After the laser treatment, the doctor prescribed …

The outpatient staff were all polite and courteous, which was impressive, until we met one doctor who didn't even glance at us when we greeted him. He turned to ask my husband what was wrong and what he needed help with. I wondered why, as long as it wasn't considered honorable for a doctor. 😅 I let that slide; we reciprocated the respect he showed us. However, what was unacceptable was that after removing the polyp from my husband's head, the doctor didn't inform the patient about wound care, how many days to wait, what medication to use for pain, or when the dressing should be removed. We had to ask the staff outside the clinic ourselves. I'd like to tell this doctor: please don't rush to dismiss patients after treatment; it's unprofessional and damages the hospital's reputation.
